ambiguity_interpretations.detail: The Docker analog reverts two layers in a scratch wrapper copy (bind-mounts the sibling AND substitutes a Landlock passthrough for the inner adapter). This is the faithful analog of the native control (which omits exactly the layer under test): inner Landlock would deny the read regardless of mounts, so isolating the mount layer requires bypassing Landlock; the probe exiting 40 proves the bytes are genuinely reachable once the boundary is omitted. Load-bearing assertion preserved, not weakened; omission containers are scratch-only per non-goals.

Guard reads capabilities via capget(2) version 2 because v3 returns EINVAL on this kernel/user pair; v2 covers caps 0-31 and with --cap-drop ALL the bounding set is empty, so no capability >=32 can be effective anyway. Minor ABI coverage limitation inherent to v2; the asserted security property (zero effective/permitted capabilities) holds.

Matches the contract signature 'ADAPTER --root TRIAL_ROOT --runner RUNNER -- RUNNER_ARGUMENTS...': arguments after -- are passed to the inner adapter, which enforces command[0]==runner before exec; flag-shaped/unknown options before -- exit 2 before any docker invocation (verified independently, evidence 06).

The contract files_modify purposes scope those three files to 'once gates and QA pass' (manifest, phase record) and Orchestrator ownership (run_state). A Generator-side update before Mode B and QA would contradict the purpose text. The deferral must be closed by the Orchestrator after Mode B and QA; this verdict does not close it.
